failing_checks.title: Per-action amount bound
failing_checks.reason: The client signs a transfer for whatever amount, currency and recipient the server's challenge states. No code-enforced maximum exists. The channel client likewise signs any server-chosen cumulative amount.

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: No cumulative, daily or session budget exists on any client signing path. Many small challenges are all paid.

failing_checks.title: Atomic budget accounting
failing_checks.reason: The server reads the cumulative amount here and writes it at line 312 after an async simulation. This is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Charge replay keys use the same get-then-put pattern. The client has no budget at all.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: On the client the recipient comes from the server challenge with no allowlist. The server side is operator-fixed through its recipient parameter.

failing_checks.title: Replay and double payment
failing_checks.reason: Replay and cumulative protection run only if a store is configured, and the get-then-put is racy. In the pull-mode charge, the challenge is burned before verification, so a transient failure forces a new challenge. The client has no idempotency on retry.

failing_checks.title: Incoming payment verification
failing_checks.reason: Push mode accepts any past successful transfer with a matching recipient, amount and contract. It checks no payer, memo, challenge binding or time. The dedup store is optional. Pull mode never checks the transfer's from argument or the other operations in the transaction.

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: The channel client signs bytes returned by a simulation of a server-chosen channel contract. It checks neither the channel address nor the cumulative amount. The server-side pull-mode path does inspect operations through verifySacInvocation, but the client path does not.

failing_checks.title: Raw byte signing
failing_checks.reason: The key signs bytes that come from the contract the challenge names. A malicious contract can return any bytes to be signed.

failing_checks.title: Network and endpoint pinning
failing_checks.reason: On the client, the challenge selects the network. That selects the passphrase and the default RPC URL. The same pattern is at src/channel/client/Channel.ts:66.

failing_checks.title: Expiry and fees
failing_checks.reason: The sponsor's fee bump max fee is ten times the client-supplied inner fee. The inner timebounds are never checked, so an inner transaction with no expiry is accepted and sponsored. The clients' own transactions do use setTimeout.

failing_checks.title: Submission outcome
failing_checks.reason: The send status (ERROR, TRY_AGAIN_LATER) is never checked before the code polls getTransaction. On the charge path the client then loops on NOT_FOUND until 60 attempts. A rejected send or a timeout throws an error, and a retry rebuilds the transaction instead of checking the hash. Later poll errors

failing_checks.title: Failure and rollback paths
failing_checks.reason: The challenge replay marker (line 134) and the cumulative amount are stored before the close transaction is submitted. If the close fails or times out, the cumulative amount stays advanced and the challenge is burned. The charge path also burns the challenge id (line 89) before pull-mode submission,

failing_checks.title: Approvals fail closed
failing_checks.reason: The on-chain closed-channel gate passes when the RPC call errors, so it fails open.

failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: A push-mode proof, which is a transaction hash, is not bound to the payer or the challenge. Any past matching transfer can be accepted. The channel replay protection is also skipped when no store is configured.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: Safety controls (replay, cumulative state) are optional or fail open. The client signs whatever the challenge asks, with no limit in code.

failing_checks.title: Stated purpose versus behaviour
failing_checks.reason: The comment says the check mirrors a dispute guard, but it fails open. The commitment is never compared to the channel balance.

failing_checks.title: Core function works
failing_checks.reason: The sendTransaction status is not checked, and state is committed before the close is submitted. Errors after the send surface as failures.
